newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes weaker, Brent trades at Dec - 57 cents.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes weaker, Brent trades at Dec - 57 cents.

text.p: North Sea physical crude markets remained in the doldrums on Wednesday with differentials easing despite a rise in outright levels with stronger Brent futures, traders said.
A Brent cargo loading Nov 14-16 traded at Dec Brent -57 cents, after the seller failed to attract bids at Dec Brent -50 cents.
Dec Brent was trading nearly 30 cents higher around IPE screen levels of $22.45/$22.50 by 1820 GMT.
A number of mid-Nov Brent cargoes remain unsold, traders said.
"It's the Brent overhang that's really weighing us down," said one trader.
Several Brent cargoes remained in the hands of a major while another four were held by a trader.
The trader declined to discuss speculation that it was working a large cargo out of the region.
A weak Brent/WTI spread was keeping the transatlantic arbitrage window firmly shut, dealers said.
BP and JP Morgan kept two of the three Brent cargoes which were nominated from the paper chains on Wednesday. The third was left with Shell UK at the five o'clock deadline.
Other North Sea grades also weakened. Norwegian Ekofisk traded at Dated Brent +12 cents for a Nov 24 loader, and at Dated Brent +10 cents for a cargo loading Nov 30-Dec 2.

Most grades were still showing for November with third decade Statfjord barely touched yet. A seller of Statfjord was offering a 20-24 Nov cargo at Dated Brent +20 cents but bids were below double figures, traders said.
Oseberg was in shorter supply after two prompt cargoes moved on Tuesday at lower values of Brent +15 cents.
On the paper market, a cfd for next week traded lower at Dec -34 cents.
